hero.title: The Velvet Table
hero.headline: Gastronomic excellence
hero.subtitle: Cooking from the coast and the garden, told with very little. In the heart of Chiado.

about.title: Velvet in Chiado
about.p1: The Velvet Table opened in Lisbon in 2016, in a Chiado house where the light stays low and the service stays quiet. The name belongs to the room: a quiet table, and plates built around a few ingredients, chosen for the season and for the hand that grew them.
about.p2: Mateo Alves’ cooking joins Portuguese memory with the discipline of a European dining room. Atlantic fish, inland gardens, slow fermentations. Nothing is added unless it serves the flavour.
about.p3: In 2023 the Michelin Guide awarded the restaurant a star. The pace of the house did not change: two services, few seats, a cellar built with the sommelier.
about.awardText: Michelin Guide, 2023. Twenty-eight seats and a menu that moves with the sea.

experiences.title: How dinner works here
experiences.intro: The main room, a private room and a cellar meant to accompany the plate, not cover it.

private.title: Private dining
private.text: A room for tables of up to fourteen. The menu is agreed in advance, with its own service and your own hour.
private.long: The private room looks onto the inner courtyard. Book at least ten days ahead and build the menu with the kitchen: the house tasting menu, or a sequence written for the occasion. The sommelier can prepare a pairing or work from bottles you bring.

seasonal.title: Seasonal menu
seasonal.text: A short sequence that follows the garden and the tides. It stays on the carte for a few weeks, then leaves.
seasonal.long: Each season we publish a five-course menu beside the long tasting. It is the most direct way to read what entered the kitchen that week: coastal shellfish, vegetables from a single grower, a dessert built on one fruit.

wine.title: Wine pairing
wine.text: Five glasses with the tasting menu. Atlantic wines, a few Italian bottles, no rigid sequence.
wine.long: Rafael Costa builds the pairing on the day’s menu, not on a fixed list. It often opens with a Bairrada sparkling wine and closes on a small sweet wine. The pairing is optional and should be noted when you book.

mateo.name: Mateo Alves
mateo.bio: Raised between Lisbon and Piedmont. He has led the kitchen since opening day, with a brigade of eight.

ines.name: Inês Carvalho
ines.bio: She looks after the main courses and the savoury larder. She worked in Porto before joining the house in 2019.

rafael.name: Rafael Costa
rafael.bio: He keeps a short cellar, centred on the Atlantic and on a few Italian and French regions.

sofia.name: Sofia Mendes
sofia.bio: She welcomes the room and holds the book. The pace of service, from the first glass to coffee, is hers.

menu.title: This season’s carte
menu.intro: Three readings of the same kitchen. The tasting menu is the path of the house; the carte is shorter; the wines follow the plate.
menu.tastingNote: Seven courses. Drinks not included. The menu is served for the whole table.
menu.wineNote: Price by the glass and by the bottle. Ask the room for the full list.

oyster.name: Oyster crystal
oyster.description: Oyster, cucumber, dill and a cold green-apple broth.
oyster.detail: It opens the menu. The oyster stays raw; the cucumber is pressed until it is almost clear.

egg.name: The house egg
egg.description: A low-temperature egg, seasonal truffle and a clear chicken broth.
egg.detail: One egg, cooked for an hour. Truffle is used only when it is truly in season.

urchin.name: Sea urchin and cauliflower
urchin.description: Sea urchin, cauliflower cream and lemon zest.
urchin.detail: The urchin arrives in the morning from Sesimbra. Cauliflower softens the dish without hiding the sea.

turbot.name: Turbot
turbot.description: Roasted turbot, clams and brown butter.
turbot.detail: Cooked on the skin and finished at the last moment. The clams open in their own liquor.

lamb.name: Lamb and artichoke
lamb.description: Lamb shoulder, artichoke, olives and roasting juices.
lamb.detail: The shoulder cooks for a long time. The artichoke is raw at the centre and braised at the edge.

chocolate.name: Chocolate and oil
chocolate.description: Seventy-percent chocolate, new oil and salt.
chocolate.detail: A small dessert. The oil is from an Alentejo mill, added cold.

prawn.name: Red prawn
prawn.description: Red prawn crudo, citrus and a delicate oil.
prawn.detail: Served cold, with a lightly acidic dressing. Ask for the day’s origin.

burrata.name: Burrata and tomato
burrata.description: Burrata, late tomato and basil, when the garden allows.
burrata.detail: Out of season the tomato becomes a clear broth. The burrata stays.

risotto.name: Saffron risotto
risotto.description: Rice, saffron, bone marrow and a reduced stock.
risotto.detail: Stirred slowly. The saffron is threads, not powder.

octopus.name: Octopus
octopus.description: Roasted octopus, smoked potato and parsley.
octopus.detail: Cooked gently and finished over embers. The potato is crushed, not fried.

duck.name: Duck
duck.detail: The breast stays pink. The plum is cooked in the juices, with no added sugar.

lemon.name: Lemon tart
lemon.description: Lemon cream, shortcrust and a thin meringue.
lemon.detail: A house dessert, more sharp than sweet. It is made in the morning.

bairrada.name: Bairrada sparkling
bairrada.description: Dry bubbles from Baga. The house aperitif.
bairrada.detail: Traditional method, low dosage. It is the glass with which we open almost every table.

encruzado.name: Encruzado, Dão
encruzado.description: A still white, citrus and stone. For crudo and first courses.
encruzado.detail: A young bottle, deliberately simple. It sits well with turbot and the risotto.

douro.name: Douro red
douro.description: A medium red, dark fruit and a gentle tannin.
douro.detail: Chosen for the lamb and the duck. It does not cover the roasting juices.

barolo.name: Barolo
barolo.description: An Italian selection, for guests who want to stay at the table.
barolo.detail: The vintage in the room changes. Ask Rafael before you order the bottle.

champagne.name: Champagne Blanc de Blancs
champagne.description: Chardonnay, a fine bead, a long finish.
champagne.detail: A bottle to share at the start, or with dessert if you would rather not close on a sweet wine.

privacy: This is a sample privacy note for the Velvet Table demonstration site. It is not a legal document prepared for a real business.

Details sent through the reservation form — name, email, date, time, party size and notes — are used only to reply to the table request. A newsletter address is used for the messages described on the form.

You can ask for access, correction or deletion by writing to reservas@thevelvettable.pt. The site does not sell data. If audience tools are configured, their identifiers live in the project environment.
terms: A request sent from the site is not a confirmed reservation. The table is held only after the restaurant replies.
To cancel, write or call before 15:00 on the previous day. Larger tables and private dinners may follow different terms, sent in advance.
The menu can change with the day’s market. Tell us about allergies in the form and again in the room: the kitchen works with nuts, shellfish and flour.
